title: This Tiny Sea Snail's Shell Is Dissolving While It's Alive
subject: sea butterfly pteropod

scenes.text: A tiny sea snail swims through open water. Its shell is dissolving while it's alive.
It's the sea butterfly, no bigger than half an inch, floating freely in the ocean.
In a lab, a shell dissolved in highly acidic seawater in just 45 days.
Off the US west coast, NOAA found 53 percent of the ones it sampled had severely dissolved shells.
Pink salmon, mackerel and herring eat them. A thin shell means a thinner food chain.
Carbon dioxide is making seawater more corrosive. A tiny snail, losing its shell.
